newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong golds ends down on overseas sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong golds ends down on overseas sales.

text.p: Hong Kong gold dipped on Monday, ending below New York's Friday close in drab trade as bearishness returned to bullion after U.S. stock markets steadied.
Gold dropped slightly on selling from Australia, possibly from producers, and afternoon selling interest from Europe, bullion dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$368.40/90 an ounce, off New York's US$368.70/369.20 close on Friday and down from Saturday's local close at $369.10/60.
Traders saw gold again testing lower levels, with estimates varying from $366 to $368 per ounce.
"There was no follow-through from Friday's buying," said one trader at an international bank.
Gold benefited when stock markets in the United States and Asia plunged on Friday on comments by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan that equities could be overheated.
Local gold ended HK$4 lower at HK$3,405 a tael and continued to trade at a premium over the spot price.
Traders reported some physical buying, but noted it was not spectacular.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to +3.00 from its previous fix at +5.00.
